claim: An edit drafted against an agent page that moves mid-session is written beside the page's old path and is then invisible: `akasha change list` answers a smaller number, exits nought and refuses nothing, so a lost edit reads exactly like having drafted fewer. Every call resolves the sidecar afresh through the index, and `keptEdits` remakes whatever folder that names, so a draft whose page moved a second earlier reads an empty prior fold and appends alone at the vacated path. Nothing compares what one call was told it kept against what the next call finds. The same silence covers the clear after a landing: `droppedFirst` returns without a word where the lines it goes to drop are not the lines it finds, so edits that did land stay listed. Three agents hit this on 2026-09-13. Three stranded sidecars sit at the vacated path, one row each, each written a second after its own page's move commit.

evidence:
Read and measured 2026-09-13 at HEAD. The loss is reported rather than observed: the window had closed before I looked. What is observed is the residue and its timing; the rest is read.

THE MOVE. Fourteen commits titled `subagent pages move under agent/subagent/pages/` land between 09:13:59 and 09:17:20 on 2026-09-13, each renaming two to four `.subagent.ts` files out of `seat-system/subagent/pages/`. Only tracked page files appear in them; the git-ignored sidecar beside a page is carried along and appears in no commit. The sweep is unfinished: forty-one subagent pages are tracked under the new root and six under the old, new ones are still born under the old, and my own page moved at 09:28:47 while this was written, so the window is still open.

HOW A DRAFT GOES TO THE OLD PATH. Draft, list and apply are three processes, each resolving the agent's page afresh: `change-draft.command.code.ts:77`, `change-list.command.code.ts:15`, `change-apply.command.code.ts:43` and `apply-running.module.code.ts:146` all call `agentPathOf`, which falls through at `warranting.module.code.ts:365-367` to `subagentPathOf` at `:352-363`, reading `listedAt(root, "subagent", slug)[0]` and never the disk. `editsAt` at `edits-keeping.module.code.ts:41-47` derives the sidecar name from that page path, no disk either. `keptEdits` at `:273-290` locks the derived path and `mkdirSync(dirname(full), { recursive: true })` at `:281` remakes the folder the move emptied; `heldIn` at `:283` then reads nothing there, so `had` is empty and `settled` at `:249-261` appends the new row alone. A later list calls `listingKept` at `change-acting.module.code.ts:261-267`, reading `editsIn` at the path the index now names. Neither compares what it found against anything asked for. The one signal is `keptSaid` at `change-running.module.code.ts:328-330`, printed at `:421` and `:433`: the answer names the path the edits are kept at. It is a path in prose, and the exit is nought.

THE RESIDUE AND ITS TIMING. Three sidecars sit at the vacated root whose ids' pages are now under the new one. Each was written one to two seconds after the commit that moved its own page, and each holds exactly one row — what an empty `had` produces. Under `seat-system/subagent/pages/`: `ember-ae9e180fbf0bb2cd1`, 1426 bytes, 09:15:34.74, against `c347f5d2b31` at 09:15:33; `athena-ab5c1d7ca25d6c244`, 721 bytes, 09:16:41.72, against `8b463329fe0` at 09:16:41; `athena-a498c748bb4ee1a35`, 771 bytes, 09:17:21.66, against `0d482ad901c` at 09:17:20. No edits sidecar sits beside any of the three at the new root.

EACH HOLDS WORK THAT LANDED OR WAS OVERTAKEN. The ember row's `contentTo` is in `temper/lost-treasure/modules/lost-treasure-item-cache/lost-treasure-item-cache.module.code.ts` now, landed by `5736a590bc7`. The athena-ab5c row adds a test to `command/pages/change/draft/change-draft.command.test.ts`, and that test is in the file now. The athena-a498 row empties the intents of `athena-command-modules.initiative.ts`, a page removed whole at `26bd524ff65`. Two were re-drafted and landed, one overtaken; none needs re-landing and nothing was cleared.

THEY ARE ORPHANED RATHER THAN PENDING. `subagent.page-type.ts:51-55` says the edits a subagent leaves unlanded move onto the seat that dispatched it as its page goes. That carry is `movedOnto` at `subagent-recovering.module.code.ts:74-88`, reading `linesIn(root, subagentPage)`, where `subagentPage` comes from `subagentPagesStanding` at `agent-page-reading.module.code.ts:39-53`, which walks the index. The carry reads the same resolved path the loss stranded the edit away from, so a stranded sidecar migrates nowhere. Read rather than run.

WHAT IS LIVE AT THAT ROOT, AND IS NOT RESIDUE. Subagent pages are tracked there too, born after the sweep began and not yet swept, one of them with an edits sidecar that was growing while this was written. Those are working agents the sweep has not reached, and the set turns over by the minute.

THE SECOND SITE, READ AND NOT OBSERVED. An agent reports an apply that landed a real commit and left all twelve edits listed, its next draft then refused because edit one no longer fit its body. I did not see that run. The code holds a second silent return of the same shape: `undone` at `apply-running.module.code.ts:122-128` clears the kept edits through `droppedFirst` after `applying` has committed, and `droppedFirst` at `edits-keeping.module.code.ts:222-239` re-reads the sidecar from disk and returns without a word twice, where `held.length < went.length` at `:229` and where any of the first `went.length` lines differs at `:230`. A clear that did not happen is reported as a landing that did. That is the clear after a landing rather than the resolve before a draft, filed here because the absence is one.

WHAT I DID NOT VERIFY. I did not reproduce the loss; the window had closed. Its evidence is two independent agent reports hours apart plus the code path and the residue above, not an observed failure. I did not see a listing answer four where five were drafted; that count is one agent's report. The tree does not say how many rows those three ids held at the new root when their pages moved, so it does not say how large any one loss was. I did not establish that the fourth agent's uncleared edits came from a move, only that both of `droppedFirst`'s returns are silent.

NEAR PAGES THAT DO NOT BIND THIS. `a-folder-move-leaves-a-running-writer-appending-to-the-path-it-already-resolved` has the same occasion and stops at the tree being wrong rather than at an edit going missing.

THE CONDITION A MEND WOULD MEET: a call that keeps edits says how many it holds, and a later call can tell a smaller number apart from a smaller draft. Described rather than built.
